description: ODC (EDIT and REFACTOR coverage of consumed REST): work on a REST client that THIS job did not create. The base is job:rest-consume-post, that is, the IRestClient WfCovOrdersApi, the two IRestStructure and the POST method WfCovCreateOrder already exist when the first op runs - there is no client or structure create here on purpose, because creating and configuring in the same job proves no maintenance at all. The four changes are all made on top of state that the OTHER job left written: (1) change the BaseURL of the inherited client and the TimeoutinSeconds of the inherited method, (2) ADD a GET method to the inherited client reusing the inherited response structure, (3) give the inherited method a REAL consumer - a server action that invokes it with IExecuteServerActionNode - and only then (4) rename the method and the client, to see what the platform rewrites on its own and what is left behind. Outside the job that created them there are no aliases: the client is cited as 'IRestClient:Name', the method as 'IRestAction:Name' and a child by the path 'IRestClient:Name/Child'. Each change has its get BEFORE and its get AFTER. Username and Password are NOT written: in ODC both properties exist in the API and accept writes, but Verify refuses them as an ERROR (already measured in rest-consume-post.json); what stays in the model is the MODE (AuthenticationType/ClientAuthentication), and this job reads it back intact to show that editing the BaseURL does not touch it. NOTE ON THE DATA CONTRACT: an IRestClient and an IRestAction are TOP-LEVEL NAMED elements, so the eight writes of this job on them are checked at the end (BaseURL, the two TimeoutinSeconds, HTTPMethod/URLPath/ResponseFormat of the new method and the Public/Description of the action that calls) - and they are checked BY KEY, not by name, which is the only reason a job that renames the client and the method AFTER writing them still passes. What stays outside the watch is what is not top-level: the IRestActionInput/IRestActionOutput and the IRestStructure only answer to Verify and to the get/dump of this job.

expectedMessages.why: ODC: an app (CrossDevice) does not expose a public server action (the live Studio gives an error); the action stays private and without a consumer in this proof job

ops.name: WfCovOrdersApi
ops._why: (0) INHERITED STARTING POINT: the REST client already exists before the first op of this job. It came from job:rest-consume-post, not from a create here

(1) BEFORE, the client: BaseURL https://api.example.com, AuthenticationType BasicAuthentication with ClientAuthentication SendAsBasicAuthHeader, Actions 1, Structures 2, ExtendedProperties 1. Note Username and Password at NULL: it is not an omission of this job, it is the platform rule - in ODC the credentials do not live in the model

(2) BEFORE, the whole inherited tree: the fixed header Accept, the structures WfCovOrderRequest/WfCovOrderResponse and the method WfCovCreateOrder with its four parameters. This is the snapshot the final dump is compared with
(3) BEFORE, the inherited method: POST /orders, RequestFormat and ResponseFormat JSON, TimeoutinSeconds 30 written by the other job
(4) BEFORE, who calls it: nobody. count 0 - a REST client that is created and configured has, by itself, no consumer at all. That is why part 3 of this job has to give it one before renaming it

(5a) CHANGE 1 - the BaseURL of the INHERITED client. It is the most common edit in the real life of an integration (the provider changed host or version) and the one that only a maintenance job can show: the value being replaced is not an empty field, it is what the previous job wrote there. The URLPath of the methods does not change: the effective address becomes this BaseURL + /orders
(5b) CHANGE 1, second half - the timeout is per METHOD, not on the client: the ODC IRestClient has no timeout property at all (see the get (1)). 30 -> 60 on an inherited method

(5c) AFTER, the client: compare with the get (1). The BaseURL CHANGED; AuthenticationType, ClientAuthentication, DateFormat and the Description from the other job STAYED. Editing the address does not touch the authentication mode
(5d) AFTER, the method: TimeoutinSeconds 60 and everything else equal - the POST, the /orders and the two JSON formats still belong to the other job

ops.name: WfCovGetOrder
ops._why: (6a) CHANGE 2 - ADD a method to the INHERITED client. The parent is not a $alias: aliases are local to the job that declares them, and the one that declared this client was another job. Outside it the stable reference is 'IRestClient:WfCovOrdersApi'
the {Id} is only substituted if the input is UrlPlacement; without that the method compiles and calls the wrong address
only ResponseFormat: a GET carries no body, so there is no RequestFormat to define - it is the contract difference between this method and the inherited POST
the same timeout as the already corrected inherited method: it is per method, so a new method inherits nothing from its neighbor

THE PROOF OF CHANGE 2: the NEW method types its response with the INHERITED structure, created by the other job. Reusing what is already in the client is what distinguishes adding a method from creating another client beside it

(6b) AFTER: the new method, with the GET, the parameterized URLPath and the timeout. Note the RequestFormat: it reads 'None', not empty - this job never wrote anything to it, and None is the value a method is born with; compare with the get (3), where the inherited method says JSON because the other job wrote it so it would have a body. The alias $novo only exists because THIS job created it - it is the difference between what is inherited and what is added
(6c) AFTER, the client again: Actions went from 1 to 2 and Structures is still 2 - the new method entered the inherited client without duplicating any structure

ops.name: WfCov_Order_Place
ops._why: (7a) CHANGE 3 - give the inherited method a REAL CONSUMER. Without this the rename in part 4 proved nothing: renaming an object that nobody calls never breaks anyone

ops.value: Cria uma encomenda no servico externo. Escrita por rest-consume-lifecycle.json para dar um consumidor real ao metodo herdado.

ops._why: the local variable is typed by the INHERITED structure of the REST client: an IRestStructure is a module type like any other, cited by name

ops.name: Start
ops._why: a raw IServerAction is not born with terminals (unlike the IRestServiceAction of the exposed REST): the job creates them
Assign has no Name: what appears in the flow is the Label

ops.name: WfCovCreateOrder
ops._why: the node deliberately receives the SAME name as the inherited method, which is what Studio does when the method is dragged into the flow. It is this coincidence that part 4 puts to the test: the node name only follows the rename when it was equal to that of the target (in refactor-inherited.json, where the author called the node 'Describe', it did not follow)
it is THIS set that makes the call exist: the node points to the inherited REST method by Type:Name, just as it would point to a server action of its own
argument by the name of the method input (Request, BodyPlacement and IsMandatory): without a value, a mandatory input gives a Verify error
the other inherited mandatory input, the one for the X-Api-Key header. The argument name is the OutSystems name of the parameter, not the OriginalName with hyphens
the response is read by the NODE NAME, not by the method's: <Node>.<Output>.<Attribute>. Keep this line - it is what part 4 will read back after the rename
(7b) AFTER: compare with the usages (4), which gave zero. The inherited method now has a REAL consumer, the Execute node of WfCov_Order_Place. Only from here on does renaming cost anything

ops.name: WfCovPlaceOrder
ops._why: (8a) CHANGE 4 - RENAME THE INHERITED METHOD WITH A CONSUMER LINKED. The name said Create but the service calls it place order. It returns consumers 1 (the Execute node) and expressionsRewritten 0 - and the zero is a LIE by omission: the expression WfCovCreateOrder.Response.Id exists and will indeed be rewritten, but what counts as a consumer is the NODE, not the expression that reads the node. Whoever trusts this number concludes there is nothing to review. The proof is in the next three ops, not here

(8b) the method now answers to the new name, with the SAME key as the get (3) (HNbcF5mFNkGN8pfMpbd9ug) and with the TimeoutinSeconds 60 from change 1 intact: renaming does not rewrite configuration. Referrers went to 1 - and it is the consumer from change 3

(8c) WHAT FOLLOWED, first part: the consumer NODE, with the SAME key as (7b). It changed name on its own - and that is why this path already finds it as WfCovPlaceOrder - because it was named exactly like the method. In refactor-inherited.json, where the author called the node 'Describe', the name did NOT follow: what the platform rewrites is the name it had put there itself

(8d) WHAT FOLLOWED, the central proof and the reason the counter is no use: the Assign expression now says WfCovPlaceOrder.Response.Id, without a single manual fix, despite the expressionsRewritten 0 of op (8a). It is the lane difference measured in AGENTS.md: in the O11 lane this same expression would keep the old name and the module would fail with ExpressionUnknownObject: Can't identify 'WfCovCreateOrder' element in expression. Always compare by the dump, never by the number - in both lanes it gives zero and the two lanes do opposite things. Note also that the arguments (Body, ApiKey) did not move: renaming the method does not touch the names of its parameters
(8e) the consumer is the SAME object as in (7b), with the same key: the name of the target changed, not who calls it

(9a) BEFORE renaming the CLIENT: count 0, and with two methods inside it, one of them called by an action. The contrast with (7b) is the point - whoever calls an integration points to the METHOD, never to the client; the client is only the house where it lives

ops.name: WfCovSalesApi
ops._why: (9b) RENAME THE INHERITED CLIENT. It returns consumers 0 and here the zero is honest: no expression, no node and no argument cites the client name. It is the change that looks the most frightening of the four and the cheapest INSIDE the module - outside it is still not free, because it is by this name that the service appears in the portal and in the logs
(9c) AFTER: same key as the get (1), new name, and the BaseURL from change 1, the authentication mode and the counts (Actions 2, Structures 2) all untouched

ops.name: WfCovOrdersApi
ops._why: (9d) empty list: the inherited name disappeared from the module

(9e) WHAT STAYED INTACT: the consumer node has the same key and the same Action as (8c). Renaming the house does not touch whoever calls the resident - which is why renaming the client is safe and renaming the method is the one that requires reading the flow back
(10) WHAT STAYED: the method added in change 2 remains exactly as it was after the two renames, and now inside a client with another name

(11) The final tree, to put next to the dump (2): the same Accept header with the same expression, the same two inherited structures (none duplicated to serve the new method) and the inherited method already with the new name and its four parameters intact. The added method appears FIRST, not at the end: the children of a REST client are not an author sequence - already in the dump (2) the WfCovOrderResponse came before the WfCovOrderRequest, although it was created later. Whoever wants an order chosen by themselves has it in the attributes of an entity (op move), not here
